data.one_liner: Implement and manage foreground services on Android and iOS platforms.
data.what_it_does: This plugin allows you to run long-running repetitive tasks in a foreground service with continuous notification support. It provides two-way communication between the background task handler and the main UI isolate, along with automatic restart capabilities.
use_when: You need to execute repetitive background tasks that shouldn't be killed immediately when the app is minimized
You want to display an ongoing notification for a persistent service on Android and iOS
avoid_when: You only need simple short-lived asynchronous background tasks
You want a fully cross-platform solution without platform-specific manifest or Info.plist configuration
strengths: Supports two-way communication between the background task and the main UI
Provides options to automatically resume the foreground service on boot or package update
Includes utilities for handling battery optimizations and notifications
weaknesses: Requires manual configuration of platform-specific permissions, Gradle files, and Android Manifest services
iOS background execution is heavily limited by the operating system
data.setup_notes: Requires modifying AndroidManifest.xml with specific foreground service types and permissions, setting up Gradle and Kotlin versions, configuring Info.plist on iOS, and setting the plugin registrant callback in AppDelegate.
